target.statement: DROD achieves AUC 0.8330 on synthetic dataset D1 (clusterliers only), the best among 9 methods
target.table_ref: Table V, row D1, column DROD
target.dataset: D1 (synthetic, 1000 normal samples + 2 clusterliers of 100 points each, generated from base dataset C1)

compute.basis: DROD is a pure-Python k-d-tree / graph algorithm on ~1200 2-D points with T=60 samplings; the paper reports CPU-only runs (i7, 32GB), so a laptop finishes in minutes once the repo's D1 generator and scoring code are wired up, but the synthetic generator details (Gaussian means/variances for clusterliers) are only partially specified, so some re-implementation/verification is needed.

blockers: Synthetic D1 generation parameters (clusterlier Gaussian mean/variance) are only loosely described; exact reproduction of 0.8330 may require tuning
Repo may not ship the exact D1 generator/config used for Table V
title: Hierarchical Reference Sets for Robust Unsupervised Detection of Scattered and Clustered Outliers
